ai-at-work.title: Google justifies its massive AI spending with a booming cloud business
ai-at-work.excerpt: Google's cloud business is thriving, as companies adopting its AI and AI infrastructure services help the tech giant to report record profits.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google's cloud division is firing on all cylinders, with AI adoption driving record profits that justify the company's massive spending on AI infrastructure and services. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because it signals that enterprise AI tooling is moving from experiment to mainstream, meaning your organization needs a real strategy around which AI services to standardize on. The irony is delicious: Google's betting the farm on AI while most enterprises are still figuring out how to stop employees from accidentally leaking proprietary data into ChatGPT.

ai-at-work.title: Treasury threatens sanctions after White House claims Moonshot distilled Anthropic’s Fable
ai-at-work.excerpt: The episode has also intensified a broader debate in Washington over the influx of Chinese open models.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: The White House claimed its Moonshot AI distilled Anthropic's Claude model, and now the Treasury Department is threatening sanctions over alleged technology transfer violations. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals how seriously government agencies are scrutinizing AI model provenance and international data flows, which directly impacts enterprise AI adoption policies and compliance requirements. Here's the kicker: we're apparently living in a world where AI models need their own passports now, and your compliance team better start reading the fine print on every foundation model your company touches.

ai-at-work.title: How OpenAI’s human mistake led to the AI-powered hack on Hugging Face
ai-at-work.excerpt: OpenAI made a mistake setting up what it called a “highly isolated” testing environment and sandbox. According to cybersecurity experts, that human mistake is what made the AI-powered attack on Huggin
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI's poorly configured sandbox environment became the vector for an AI-powered attack on Hugging Face, proving that even the smartest AI companies can botch basic security hygiene. This matters to workplace IT teams because it's a stark reminder that AI tools are only as secure as the infrastructure supporting them, and bad setup beats good intentions every single time. After thirty years in this space, I can tell you that "highly isolated" sandbox is corporate speak for "we didn't actually isolate it," and it's the same mistake we've been watching companies make since the early 2000s.

ai-at-work.title: Yope raises $12.3M to build a private social network without algorithms or ads
ai-at-work.excerpt: Yope, a fast-growing social app focused on private groups of friends and family, has raised $12.3 million in seed funding. Instead of chasing creators and algorithmic feeds, the startup is betting tha
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Yope just landed 12.3 million dollars to build a private social network that ditches algorithms and ads in favor of small group messaging and photo sharing. This matters to digital workplace folks because it signals what workers actually want: controlled, distraction-free spaces where real humans connect instead of fighting infinite feeds and engagement games. My take? It's refreshing, but let's see if they can actually stay ad-free when growth eventually hits the capital wall.

tools-tech.title: Firefox 153 enables Containers by default, and you can create your own - here's how
tools-tech.excerpt: Containers are a boon to your browsing security and privacy. Out of the box, Firefox now gives you four pre-configured containers: Personal, Work, Banking, and Shopping.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Firefox 153 just activated Containers by default, giving users four pre-built isolation zones for different browsing activities. This matters because digital workplace folks deal with constant security theatre and compliance audits, and now you've got a legitimate technical control that actually works without extra clicks. Honestly, it's wild that it took until 2024 for a major browser to make this the default, but better late than never when you're juggling seventeen work tabs that shouldn't know about each other.

tools-tech.title: Monday.com cuts 20% of its workforce to restructure for the AI era
tools-tech.excerpt: Healthy software companies typically don’t suddenly eliminate one-fifth of their workforce, but monday.com is doing just that as it bets on flatter teams, AI agents, and customer implementation expert
tools-tech.dwp_take: Monday.com just laid off 20% of its staff to restructure around AI and flatter teams, betting that automation and fewer layers will be the future of work. This matters because if a work platform company thinks its own operations need radical restructuring to survive the AI shift, that's a pretty loud signal about what enterprise customers should expect to change in their own organizations. Here's the thing: companies always say layoffs are about "restructuring for the future," but let's be honest, flatter teams and AI agents also mean fewer middle managers approving expense reports, which is the real goal here.

tools-tech.title: 10 cool things Copilot can do in PowerPoint
tools-tech.excerpt: Building a presentation can take lots of time. There are design choices to figure out: the slide layouts, fonts, theme colors, and so on. You can use a template to skip this hassle, but you still have
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft rolled out Copilot features in PowerPoint that automate design work like layout selection, font choices, and content formatting so you don't have to manually tinker with every slide. This matters because presentation creation is a genuine time sink for knowledge workers, and if AI can genuinely shave hours off that work, it's worth paying attention to. That said, I've seen plenty of "AI will save you hours" promises evaporate once people actually use the tools, so the real test is whether your team ends up with fewer bad deck-building habits or just faster bad decks.

tools-tech.title: Your instant Android backup upgrade
tools-tech.excerpt: Here in this high-tech era of 2026, keeping important info backed up and synced should be effortless and something that just happens on its own, automatically, without any actual thought or ongoing hu
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google has made Android backups more seamless and automatic, reducing the manual work users need to do to protect their data. For digital workplace pros managing BYOD programs and employee device security, this matters because easier backups mean fewer lost files and fewer support tickets from people who forgot to sync. The irony is that we've been saying "backups should just work automatically" for about 20 years now, and we're still apparently surprised when they finally do.

digital-culture.title: Workers are interested in creative AI tools. But hardly any are using them
digital-culture.excerpt: Artificial intelligence is changing how people view creativity in the workplace. While some leaders have touted the technology as improving the creative process at their companies, there are broader c
digital-culture.dwp_take: Most workers say they want creative AI tools at their disposal, but almost none have actually deployed them yet. This gap matters because it signals a real disconnect between enthusiasm and execution, which means your organization probably has the same tools sitting in your tech stack that nobody's trained to use properly. The truth is people always want the shiny new thing until they realize someone has to actually integrate it into their workflow, and that someone is usually already drowning in other stuff.

digital-culture.title: 5 bad management behaviors that drive good employees away
digital-culture.excerpt: Whenever I coach managers or speak to executives, I simplify leadership down to its most practical expression: helping people succeed. Employees do their best work when they have the tools, support, c
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company ran a piece on five management behaviors that cause good employees to bolt, focusing on how managers who fail to provide tools, support, clarity, development, and encouragement watch their teams wither. This matters because digital workplace leaders are uniquely positioned to either enable or obstruct these essentials, and remote work makes invisible bad management even more damaging. Here's the thing though: every single one of these "bad behaviors" boils down to managers not actually doing their job, which suggests the real problem isn't mystifying leadership but rather accountability.

digital-culture.title: China’s Open AI Models Are Challenging Silicon Valley’s Playbook
digital-culture.excerpt: As access to Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s frontier models becomes more restricted, Chinese labs are pitching their open-source alternatives as stable, accessible, and increasingly capable.
digital-culture.dwp_take: China's AI labs are releasing open-source models as Western companies like OpenAI and Anthropic lock down their best stuff behind paywalls and restrictions. This matters because every organization evaluating their AI strategy needs to know there are now credible alternatives that won't disappear behind gatekeeping or regulatory walls. Here's the thing: Silicon Valley spent years telling us closed models were the only safe bet, and now they're learning what happens when you make something scarce and expensive in a world where smart people actually prefer open tools.

industry-news.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE and Galaxy Tab S12 Surface in Google App Ahead of Launch
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung’s Galaxy S26 FE and Galaxy Tab S12 appeared in a Google app list, hinting at software prep before a possible late-summer launch. The post Samsung Galaxy S26 FE and Galaxy Tab S12 Surface in Go
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung's next-gen budget phone and tablet showed up in Google's app compatibility listings, suggesting the company is gearing up for a late-summer announcement. This matters because enterprise device procurement teams need to know what's coming down the pike so they can plan refresh cycles and test compatibility with their digital workplace tools before deployment. Here's the thing though: every year someone "surfaces" a Samsung device in some app list, and half the time it never materializes or lands with barely a whimper, so I'd hold off on updating your device strategy deck just yet.

industry-news.title: China Considers Export Controls on AI Models, Training Data and Chip Technology
industry-news.excerpt: China is considering tighter controls on AI models, training data, and chip designs, potentially limiting how Chinese technology reaches global users. The post China Considers Export Controls on AI Mo
industry-news.dwp_take: China is weighing export restrictions on AI models, training data, and semiconductor technology to keep advanced capabilities domestic. This matters to digital workplace pros because it could fracture the global tech supply chain and force companies to choose between market access and technology partnerships, making your infrastructure decisions a lot more complicated. If this happens, we're basically looking at a tech world with two separate playgrounds, which is great news for consultants who bill by the hour and terrible news for everyone else trying to actually get work done.

industry-news.title: Samsung Unveils Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and Fold8 at Unpacked 2026
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra and Fold8 debut at Unpacked 2026 with new cameras, AI tools, prices, and clear trade-offs for buyers choosing a foldable. The post Samsung Unveils Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra a
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung launched two new foldable phones at Unpacked 2026, the Z Fold8 Ultra and standard Fold8, featuring upgraded cameras and AI capabilities at different price points. For digital workplace professionals, foldables are moving from novelty to legitimate productivity tools that actually change how you work on mobile, especially if your job involves document review or multitasking. Honestly though, after six generations we're still asking "but do people actually want this" instead of "here's why you need this" - that's the real story Samsung should tell.

industry-news.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 Launches at $1,199 With Thinner Design
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung’s $1,199 Galaxy Z Flip8 adds a thinner design, expanded FlexWindow tools, and new AI controls while retaining the same battery and rear cameras. The post Samsung Galaxy Z Flip8 Launches at $1,
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung launched the Galaxy Z Flip8 at $1,199 with a thinner form factor, better FlexWindow features, and AI controls, though the battery and rear cameras stayed the same. For digital workplace pros evaluating mobile devices for their workforce, this matters because thinner foldables eventually mean better pocket-ability and less resistance from users who think foldables are gimmicks. The real question is whether Samsung's AI controls actually solve real work problems or if they're just more features nobody asked for stuffed into a premium device that costs more than a decent laptop.
